title: Presenting Skill Order - a tactical roguelike autobattler.
author: vorty92
selftext:
Hi all, just wanted to showcase the game I'm working on here.

Wouldn't be possible without the help of Gemini. Next steps are to improve the quality/consistency of AI generated pieces of art with the rest of the project, for which I'm considering used Retro Diffusion.

Before that, I'm attempting to validate the concept and see if there's interest for a project like this.

  
If you're interested in the project, you can check it out more about it on the [Steam page](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3906750/Skill_Order/). Wishlists would be greatly appreciated at this stage.

  
If anyone has any questions regarding use/impact of AI beyond what's already disclosed on the page, I'm happy to answer any questions you may have.

I've used AI, specifically Gemini, for:  
\- Backgrounds + props (pillars)  
\- Marketing assets  
\- Druid bear form (although I manually redrew it at the appropriate size, cleaned it up and split it into an atlas)  
\- Some minor icons

  
Also open to feedback in general.

  
Thank you for your time!

comments.author: irateas
comments.body: Looks great 👍 What engine did you used?

comments.author: RelapseCatAddict
comments.body: The sound effects for the UI and buttons is perfect

comments.author: sense-net-mccoy
comments.body:
I really like the animations on your sprites. Nice work. Also the title image is killer.

My one piece of criticism, if you are serious about making this a commercial product, is that the settings looks very generic. I mean, the enemies are called "skelly". If I were you, I would find some kind of world/narrative designer to help create a unique setting. I think it would add a second source of appeal to your game besides the mechanics.

replies.author: vorty92
replies.body:
Characters and most of their animations are from an asset pack, but thank you!

  
As for the rest, this is still an initial demo with placeholder enemies created from the same pack to validate the concept. I'm a solo dev with limited resources and while I intend to improve on the topics you mentioned, hirring a world/narrative designer would be detrimental since they'd essentially only create more work.

I am open to partnering up with an artist who would expand the visuals of the game, but good rev-share pixel artists are hard to find.

comments.author: duckhunt420
comments.body: I think you need something that makes it stand out. There are a lot of games like this.. what's the special "hook" of this one?

replies.author: vorty92
replies.body: I can see some similarities in several potential directions. Which games like this are you referring to? If I understand what you mean, I can tell you what to me seem like significant differences.
